requirement:
The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
in `used`, as described in {cite}`requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description`.
rationale:
The subject's obligations are covered by `crates/trust-but-verify/src/agent/project_sources.rs#mod[tests]/fn[search_obligations_follow_delivery_and_keep_the_original_snapshot]`, which carries the `{test}` reference. I did not read the implementation.

- **First delivery includes `instructions`, even with empty `matches`.**
  - `session` first runs a failing `search_text` (pattern `(`). It then runs `search_text` for `absent`, which has no matches. The test reads `empty["instructions"].as_str().unwrap()` and checks it for phrases.
  - `peer` makes `search_structure` its first delivery. That result has `matches == []` and `page["instructions"] == instructions`.
  - `fresh` makes a non-empty `search_text` its first delivery, and `hits["instructions"] == instructions`.
- **Text and structural searches share the rule.** Both `search_text` and `search_structure` are the first delivery in different conversations, and both carry `instructions`.
- **Failed searches leave the instructions for the first successful delivery.** The invalid regex `(` fails with `is_err()`. The next successful search in the same session still carries `instructions`. The test does not run a failing structural search. That is the same shared rule, and the text-search failure covers the failure-then-first-delivery transition.
- **Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.**
  - `peer`'s later `search_text` has no `instructions`.
  - `fresh`'s `get_next_page` result has no `instructions`.
  - `session`'s second `search_text` (`hit`) has none.
  - `session`'s `get_next_page` result `second` has none.
- **Per conversation.** `session`, `fresh` and `peer` are separate `SessionTools`. Each gets its own first-delivery `instructions`, and the text is identical across them.
- **Content of the explanation.** The test asserts the instruction text contains phrases about closing delivered searches with `finish_search`, which tags to put in `used`, and `used:[]` for empty results. The detailed content is cited from `requirements.sdk.graph.search.finish_search.mcp.description`. The cited requirement's own wording and tests are not reassessed here.

No gaps found.

text: The first search result delivered in each agent conversation MUST include an
`instructions` string, even when `matches` is empty. Text and structural
searches share this rule. Failed searches leave the instructions for the first
successful delivery. Later searches and continuation pages omit the field.
The instructions explain when to call `finish_search` and which tags to include
> `Close a delivered search and record dependencies for snippets you used to
> justify your conclusion without an additional source read. search_id is the
> result's UUID and used is an array of its short entry tags, e.g.
> whose source you also read may be omitted; including them is harmless. Use
> used:[] when no entries qualify, including an empty search. Every delivered
> search must be finished before submission. The result is {search_id,
> finished:true}; no additional source is delivered.`
